                  "lineNumber": 1460,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"- Stores &amp;amp; caches:\\n  - &amp;#96;KnownDeviceStore&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;DeviceGroupStore&amp;#96; (secure archiving to Application Support)\\n  - &amp;#96;DeviceLocationCacheStore&amp;#96; (last locations + reverse geocode queue)\\n  - &amp;#96;RouteCacheStore&amp;#96; (cached &amp;#96;MKRoute&amp;#96; by device &amp;amp; transport; distance-based validity)\\n- Utilities:\\n  - &amp;#96;thisDeviceIDManager&amp;#96; (device ID generation + legacy migration)\\n  - &amp;#96;Haptic&amp;#96; (success/warning/error feedback)\\n\\n### Key Dependencies\\n- **CodeScanner**: QR code scanning functionality\\n- **MiataruAPIClient** (via local &amp;#96;Libraries/MiataruClientSwift&amp;#96;): Miataru protocol client\\n- **QRCode**: QR code generation\\n- **SwiftImageReadWrite**: Image handling utilities\\n\\n## Development Workflow\\n\\n### Code Organization\\n- **Views**: Keep UI logic minimal, delegate to managers\\n- **Managers**: Handle business logic and data persistence\\n- **Models**: Use SwiftUI's built-in data binding\\n- **Assets**: Organize by platform [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1579,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Monitor battery usage during development\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2152,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2242,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2246,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2257,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 3840,

It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;amp;#96;.\\\\n- Low Power Mode and scene phase changes are observed (e.g., &amp;amp;#96;Notification.Name.NSProcessInfoPowerStateDidChange&amp;amp;#96;) to gate animations like shimmer/pulsing without changing data behavior.\\\\n- &amp;amp;#96;iPhone_LocationStatusView&amp;amp;#96; renders &amp;amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;amp;#96; diagnostics, while &amp;amp;#96;SettingsManager&amp;amp;#96; bindings immediately adj [... omitted end of long line]"

                {
                  "lineNumber": 3514,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 3604,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 3608,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 3619,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 4657,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;DeviceLocationCacheStore&amp;#96; caches coordinates, manages a centralized reverse‑geocoding queue with a configurable distance threshold, and stores results in &amp;#96;Application Support&amp;#96;. Views consult the cache first before hitting the network and throttle UI updates to the configured map update interval.\\n- Own‑device updates trigger immediate cache writes to kick off reverse geocoding promptly. A &amp;#96;RouteCacheStore&amp;#96; caches routes by device and transport, with distance‑based invalidation.\\n- Static map elements such as &amp;#96;MiataruMapMarker&amp;#96; and &amp;#96;DeviceNameLabel&amp;#96; are rasterized and cached with keys that include color scheme and display scale; renderers respect Dynamic Type and set &amp;#96;isOpaque=false&amp;#96; where appropriate.\\n\\n## Haptic Feedback and UI Enhancements\\n**For users:**\\n- Actions like successful refresh trigger subtle haptic feedback, pulsing accuracy circles show location precision, and shimmering indica [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 4688,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Actions like successful refresh trigger subtle haptic feedback, pulsing accuracy circles show location precision, and shimmering indicators highlight loading states.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 4695,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Animations for pulsing/shimmer are automatically reduced in Low Power Mode or when the app is backgrounded to save energy.\","
                },

                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"                  \\\"content\\\": \\\"                  \\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The user reports seeing a double transition when selecting another device, which might involve two quick animation pushes. I’m considering that both the row NavigationLink and some tap gesture might lead to this, but DeviceRowView doesn’t use tap gestures in normal mode. But when returning to the list, the lastOpenedDeviceID becomes nil, which complicates things since it clears on disappearing from DeviceMapView.\\\\\\\"\\\"\""

                },

                  "lineNumber": 5824,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 5914,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 5918,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 5929,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\","
                },

                  "lineNumber": 10439,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"                  \\\"content\\\": \\\"                  \\\\\\\"content\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"The user reports seeing a double transition when selecting another device, which might involve two quick animation pushes. I’m considering that both the row NavigationLink and some tap gesture might lead to this, but DeviceRowView doesn’t use tap gestures in normal mode. The double navigation could be due to the NavigationLink to deviceID in the list and the iPhone_DeviceMapView’s onAppear setting lastOpenedDeviceID. But when returning to the list, the lastOpenedDeviceID becomes nil, which complicates things since it clears on disappearing from DeviceMapView.\\\\\\\"\\\"\""

                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"That animation was caused by the “deeplink override” logic kicking in even when you navigated normally inside the app (device map &amp;#96;.onAppear&amp;#96; sets &amp;#96;lastOpenedDeviceID&amp;#96;, which then triggered a clear/re-push).\""

                {
                  "lineNumber": 19591,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 19681,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 19685,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 19696,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 20676,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"        \\\"contents\\\": \\\"**For developers:**\\\\n- &amp;amp;#96;DeviceLocationCacheStore&amp;amp;#96; caches coordinates, manages a centralized reverse‑geocoding queue with a configurable distance threshold, and stores results in &amp;amp;#96;Application Support&amp;amp;#96;. Views consult the cache first before hitting the network and throttle UI updates to the configured map update interval.\\\\n- Own‑device updates trigger immediate cache writes to kick off reverse geocoding promptly. A &amp;amp;#96;RouteCacheStore&amp;amp;#96; caches routes by device and transport, with distance‑based invalidation.\\\\n- Static map elements such as &amp;amp;#96;MiataruMapMarker&amp;amp;#96; and &amp;amp;#96;DeviceNameLabel&amp;amp;#96; are rasterized and cached with keys that include color scheme and display scale; renderers respect Dynamic Type and set &amp;amp;#96;isOpaque=false&amp;amp;#96; where appropriate.\\\\n\\\\n## Haptic Feedback and UI Enhancements\\\\n**For users:**\\\\n- Actions like successful refresh trigger subtle  [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 20813,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"+        \\\"contents\\\": \\\"# miataru iOS App - Project Overview\\\\n\\\\n## 🎯 Project Purpose\\\\nmiataru is a privacy-focused iOS application that enables users to track their device location, share it securely with trusted parties, and manage multiple devices and groups. The app prioritizes user privacy, battery efficiency, and cross-platform compatibility.\\\\n\\\\n## 🏗️ Architecture Overview\\\\n\\\\n### Technology Stack\\\\n- **Frontend**: SwiftUI (iOS 18.0+)\\\\n- **State Management**: ObservableObject pattern with @Published properties\\\\n- **Data Persistence**: UserDefaults via SettingsManager; Application Support files for devices/groups\\\\n- **Location Services**: CoreLocation framework (foreground and significant-change background)\\\\n- **QR Code**: CodeScanner (scan), QRCode (generate)\\\\n- **Platforms**: iPhone and iPad\\\\n\\\\n### Core Components\\\\n&amp;amp;amp;#96;&amp;amp;amp;#96;&amp;amp;amp;#96;\\\\nmiataruApp.swift (Entry Point)\\\\n├── MiataruRootView (Main Navigation)\\\\n├── Onbo [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 20838,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"        \\\"contents\\\": \\\"**For developers:**\\\\n- &amp;amp;#96;DeviceLocationCacheStore&amp;amp;#96; caches coordinates, manages a centralized reverse‑geocoding queue with a configurable distance threshold, and stores results in &amp;amp;#96;Application Support&amp;amp;#96;. Views consult the cache first before hitting the network and throttle UI updates to the configured map update interval.\\\\n- Own‑device updates trigger immediate cache writes to kick off reverse geocoding promptly.                   "lineNumber": 3341,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 3431,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 3435,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 3446,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\","

                  "lineNumber": 25927,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"                  \\\"content\\\": \\\"I’m thinking that the double transition may stem from animations or interactions in the device list. The iPhone_DeviceRowView uses .transaction to potentially disable animations, which shouldn’t affect navigation. The NavigationLink and the 'selectedDeviceID' state might also play a role, although not in normal mode. I suspect the double pushes occur when the user quickly selects a device after returning from the map view. The onAppear triggers refresh notifications asynchronously, but may not directly cause navigation issues. I should implement a guard variable to prevent auto-navigation unless desired, which might help. Let's test this approach to reduce the double animation effect.\\\"\","

                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"  \\\"plan\\\": \\\"# Implementation Plan: Periodic Location Updates\\\\n\\\\n## Overview\\\\n\\\\nCurrently, &amp;amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;amp;#96; only sends location updates to the server when the location changes significantly (based on distance/accuracy thresholds). This plan adds a time-based criteria: updates will also be sent periodically at a user-configurable interval (1-24 hours), even if the location hasn't changed. This ensures battery level and other metadata stay current on the server.\\\\n\\\\n## Architecture\\\\n\\\\nThe implementation will modify the location update decision logic in &amp;amp;#96;LocationManager.swift&amp;amp;#96; to check both:\\\\n1. **Location change criteria** (existing): Distance/accuracy thresholds\\\\n2. **Time-based criteria** (new): Time elapsed since last server update\\\\n\\\\n## Implementation Details\\\\n\\\\n### 1. Add Setting for Periodic Update Interval\\\\n\\\\n**File**: &amp;amp;#96;miataru/SettingsManagers/App Settings/SettingsManager.swift&amp;amp;#96;\\\\n\\\\n-  [... omitted end of long line]"

                  "content": "+        \"contents\": \"# miataru iOS App - Project Overview\\n\\n## 🎯 Project Purpose\\nmiataru is a privacy-focused iOS application that enables users to track their device location, share it securely with trusted parties, and manage multiple devices and groups.                   "content": "+        \"contents\": \"- Unit tests for business logic\\n- UI tests for critical flows\\n- Multi-device testing\\n- Permission flow verification\\n\\n## 🔒 Privacy &amp;amp;amp; Security\\n\\n### Data Protection\\n- Location data encryption\\n- User consent requirements\\n- Data retention policies\\n- GDPR compliance\\n\\n### Permission Management\\n- Minimal permission requests\\n- Clear permission explanations\\n- Graceful permission denial\\n- User control over data\\n\\n## 📊 Performance Considerations\\n\\n### Battery Optimization\\n- Smart location updates\\n- Background task management\\n- Auto-lock control\\n- Energy-efficient operations\\n\\n### Memory Management\\n- Proper observer cleanup\\n- Weak reference usage\\n- Resource deallocation\\n- Memory leak prevention\\n\\n## 🚀 Deployment &amp;amp;amp; Distribution\\n\\n### Build Requirements\\n- Xcode 16.0+\\n- iOS 18.0+ deployment target\\n- Swift 5+\\n- macOS 14.0+ (development)\\n\\n### Distribution\\n- App Store distribution\\n- TestFlight beta testing\\n- Enterprise deploymen [... omitted end of long line]"

                {
                  "lineNumber": 9026,
                  "content": "+        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;amp;#96; constructs the &amp;amp;#96;TabView&amp;amp;#96; and hosts &amp;amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;amp;#96;, &amp;amp;#96;iPhone_Gro [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 9116,
                  "content": "+            \"text\": \"- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 9120,
                  "content": "+            \"text\": \"- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 9131,
                  "content": "+            \"text\": \"- &amp;amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;amp;#96;.\","
                }
              ]

                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"- Unit tests for business logic\\n- UI tests for critical flows\\n- Multi-device testing\\n- Permission flow verification\\n\\n## 🔒 Privacy &amp;amp; Security\\n\\n### Data Protection\\n- Location data encryption\\n- User consent requirements\\n- Data retention policies\\n- GDPR compliance\\n\\n### Permission Management\\n- Minimal permission requests\\n- Clear permission explanations\\n- Graceful permission denial\\n- User control over data\\n\\n## 📊 Performance Considerations\\n\\n### Battery Optimization\\n- Smart location updates\\n- Background task management\\n- Auto-lock control\\n- Energy-efficient operations\\n\\n### Memory Management\\n- Proper observer cleanup\\n- Weak reference usage\\n- Resource deallocation\\n- Memory leak prevention\\n\\n## 🚀 Deployment &amp;amp; Distribution\\n\\n### Build Requirements\\n- Xcode 16.0+\\n- iOS 18.0+ deployment target\\n- Swift 5+\\n- macOS 14.0+ (development)\\n\\n### Distribution\\n- App Store distribution\\n- TestFlight beta testing\\n- Enterprise deployment support [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 7972,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Improved battery optimization\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8851,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8941,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8945,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8956,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\","
                }
              ]

                  "lineNumber": 7599,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# Cursor Rules for miataru iOS App\\n\\n## Project Context\\nThis is an open-source iOS application for privacy-friendly location tracking, sharing, and device management. Built with SwiftUI and modern iOS frameworks (iOS 18 and iOS 26).\\n\\n## Code Style &amp;amp; Standards\\n- Use SwiftUI best practices\\n- Follow iOS Human Interface Guidelines\\n- Maintain privacy-first approach\\n- Use English for all code comments and strings\\n- Implement proper error handling and battery optimization\\n\\n## Architecture Guidelines\\n- Use ObservableObject and @Published for state management\\n- Keep views lightweight and delegate business logic to managers\\n- Implement proper MVVM pattern\\n- Use UserDefaults for settings persistence\\n- Handle location permissions gracefully\\n\\n## Key Components\\n- LocationManager: Handles location tracking and permissions\\n- SettingsManager: Manages user preferences\\n- Device management and QR code functionality\\n- Multi-platform support (iPhone, iPad, Mac) [... omitted end of long line]"
                },

                  "lineNumber": 7641,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Implement proper error handling and battery optimization\","

                },

                  "lineNumber": 8236,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru - App Store Description\\n\\n## Subtitle (30 characters max)\\nYour Location, Your Control\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Description (4000 characters max) + Prompt\\ntake this \\\"description text\\\" and translate these in this order: English, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, French, Italian, German, Japanese, Spanish, Simplified-Chinese \\nOutput in this language order and make each language individually copyable markdown.Each copyable markdown portion has a small note of the language before the markdown and no markdown headline itself. It should be real markdown.\\n\\nDescription Text:\\n\\nTake control of your location sharing with miataru - the privacy-focused location sharing app that puts you in charge.\\n\\nmiataru is a powerful location tracking and sharing app designed for people who value privacy and control. Share your location with family, friends, or trusted devices through your own Miataru server, keeping your data secure and under your control.\\n\\nPrivacy First:\\nYour location da [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8343,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"• See battery levels, altitude, speed, and distance for each device\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 9229,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"- Add other devices by scanning their Miataru QR code.\\n- The QR tab offers one‑tap sharing, and the add‑device sheet guides scanning and rejects non‑Miataru codes.\\n\\n- The share sheet includes additional options, and email sharing attaches the QR image reliably.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&amp;#96; renders customizable QR codes using the &amp;#96;QRCode&amp;#96; package and supports &amp;#96;ShareLink&amp;#96; and &amp;#96;MFMailComposeViewController&amp;#96;.\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_AddDeviceView&amp;#96; validates the &amp;#96;miataru://&amp;#96; prefix from scanned codes before accepting an ID and allows manual entry with color selection.\\n\\n## Onboarding Flow\\n**For users:**\\n- A six‑step wizard guides through welcome, permissions, server URL, history settings, personal QR code display, and completion.\\n- Each step shows illustrations and contextual explanations; server selection validates custom HTTPS URLs, and completion flag controls whether the wizard reappears on next launc [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 9323,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- New options include: navigation route auto‑update, route progress visualization toggle, a global pulsing/shimmer switch for map markers, and off‑screen arrow visibility.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 9356,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {\\n                HStack(alignment: .top) {\\n                    Text(\\\"•\\\")\\n                    Text(\\\"Your data stays on the server you choose for the time you choose\\\")\\n                        .multilineTextAlignment(.leading)\\n                        .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)\\n                }\\n                HStack(alignment: .top) {\\n                    Text(\\\"•\\\")\\n                    Text(\\\"Your data is only sent when you specifically activate it\\\")\\n                        .multilineTextAlignment(.leading)\\n                        .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)\\n                }\\n                HStack(alignment: .top) {\\n                    Text(\\\"•\\\")\\n                    Text(\\\"Miataru uses battery optimized background location tracking\\\")\\n                        .multilineTextAlignment(.leading)\\n                        .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical:  [... omitted end of long line]"

                {
                  "lineNumber": 9692,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru iOS App - Project Overview\\n\\n## 🎯 Project Purpose\\nmiataru is a privacy-focused iOS application that enables users to track their device location, share it securely with trusted parties, and manage multiple devices and groups. The app prioritizes user privacy, battery efficiency, and cross-platform compatibility.\\n\\n## 🏗️ Architecture Overview\\n\\n### Technology Stack\\n- **Frontend**: SwiftUI (iOS 18.0+)\\n- **State Management**: ObservableObject pattern with @Published properties\\n- **Data Persistence**: UserDefaults via SettingsManager; Application Support files for devices/groups\\n- **Location Services**: CoreLocation framework (foreground and significant-change background)\\n- **QR Code**: CodeScanner (scan), QRCode (generate)\\n- **Platforms**: iPhone and iPad\\n\\n### Core Components\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\nmiataruApp.swift (Entry Point)\\n├── MiataruRootView (Main Navigation)\\n├── OnboardingContainerView (User Setup)\\n├── LocationManagers/\\n│   └── LocationMana [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 9707,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"miataru is a privacy-focused iOS application that enables users to track their device location, share it securely with trusted parties, and manage multiple devices and groups. The app prioritizes user privacy, battery efficiency, and cross-platform compatibility.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 10126,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"• Share via email, messages, or any app\\n\\nDesigned for iOS:\\n• Native SwiftUI interface optimized for iPhone and iPad\\n• iPad multitasking support - open devices in separate windows\\n\\nBattery Conscious:\\n• Intelligent background tracking that minimizes battery drain\\n• Automatic animation reduction in Low Power Mode\\n• Smart update intervals that balance accuracy and efficiency\\n\\nSelf-Hosted Server Support:\\nConnect to your own Miataru server or choose from trusted community servers. Your location data stays where you want it - no cloud services, no data mining, no unwanted tracking.\\n\\nPerfect For:\\n• Families wanting to stay connected safely\\n• Friends sharing locations during trips\\n• People managing multiple devices\\n• Anyone who values privacy in location sharing\\n• Users who prefer self-hosted solutions\\n\\nPrivacy &amp;amp; Security:\\nmiataru is designed with privacy at its core. Your location data is only shared with the Miataru server you configure, and only [... omitted end of long line]"
                },

                  "content": "            \"text\": \"• Intelligent background tracking that minimizes battery drain\","

                  "lineNumber": 10160,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"• Automatic animation reduction in Low Power Mode\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 10235,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"Share your location securely with trusted devices. Privacy-focused, battery-optimized, and fully under your control. Connect to your own server or trusted community servers.\","
                },
                {

                  "lineNumber": 11185,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 11275,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 11279,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 11290,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\","
                },

                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"Ich möchte in der DeviceRow (iphone und ipad) gerne, wenn ein battery-wert verfügbar ist (in %) dort anstelle des Kreises ein genauso breites und mit DeviceColor eingefärbtes batteriesymbol (sfsymbols: battery.100percent ... battery.0percent) darstellen dass den Füllstand repräsentiert\""

                  "lineNumber": 12847,

Let me also check if there are any other device row implementations and look at the CachedDeviceLocation structure to understand how battery data is stored:\""

                {
                  "lineNumber": 12875,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"Now I need to update the iPhone_DeviceRowView to show the battery symbol when battery level is available. I'll replace the circle with the battery symbol when battery data is present:\""

                  "lineNumber": 12883,

                {
                  "lineNumber": 12899,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"The &amp;#96;batteryLevel&amp;#96; property will still work perfectly for our SwiftUI implementation since we're only accessing it from Swift code in the &amp;#96;iPhone_DeviceRowView&amp;#96;. The NSCoding methods will still properly encode and decode the battery level data, and the property will be available for use throughout the Swift codebase.\""

                {
                  "lineNumber": 13155,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"The user reports seeing a double transition when selecting another device, which might involve two quick animation pushes. I’m considering that both the row NavigationLink and some tap gesture might lead to this, but DeviceRowView doesn’t use tap gestures in normal mode. The double navigation could be due to the NavigationLink to deviceID in the list and the iPhone_DeviceMapView’s onAppear setting lastOpenedDeviceID. But when returning to the list, the lastOpenedDeviceID becomes nil, which complicates things since it clears on disappearing from DeviceMapView.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 13159,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I’m thinking that the double transition may stem from animations or interactions in the device list. The iPhone_DeviceRowView uses .transaction to potentially disable animations, which shouldn’t affect navigation. The NavigationLink and the 'selectedDeviceID' state might also play a role, although not in normal mode. I suspect the double pushes occur when the user quickly selects a device after returning from the map view. The onAppear triggers refresh notifications asynchronously, but may not directly cause navigation issues. I should implement a guard variable to prevent auto-navigation unless desired, which might help. Let's test this approach to reduce the double animation effect.\""

                {
                  "lineNumber": 8598,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8688,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8692,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8703,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8721,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"- Add other devices by scanning their Miataru QR code.\\n- The QR tab offers one‑tap sharing, and the add‑device sheet guides scanning and rejects non‑Miataru codes.\\n\\n- The share sheet includes additional options, and email sharing attaches the QR image reliably.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&amp;#96; renders customizable QR codes using the &amp;#96;QRCode&amp;#96; package and supports &amp;#96;ShareLink&amp;#96; and &amp;#96;MFMailComposeViewController&amp;#96;.\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_AddDeviceView&amp;#96; validates the &amp;#96;miataru://&amp;#96; prefix from scanned codes before accepting an ID and allows manual entry with color selection.\\n\\n## Onboarding Flow\\n**For users:**\\n- A six‑step wizard guides through welcome, permissions, server URL, history settings, personal QR code display, and completion.\\n- Each step shows illustrations and contextual explanations; server selection validates custom HTTPS URLs, and completion flag controls whether the wizard reappears on next launc [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8815,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- New options include: navigation route auto‑update, route progress visualization toggle, a global pulsing/shimmer switch for map markers, and off‑screen arrow visibility.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 9320,

                  "lineNumber": 14109,
                  "content": "  \"plan\": \"# Implementation Plan: Periodic Location Updates\\n\\n## Overview\\n\\nCurrently, &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; only sends location updates to the server when the location changes significantly (based on distance/accuracy thresholds). This plan adds a time-based criteria: updates will also be sent periodically at a user-configurable interval (1-24 hours), even if the location hasn't changed. This ensures battery level and other metadata stay current on the server.\\n\\n## Architecture\\n\\nThe implementation will modify the location update decision logic in &amp;#96;LocationManager.swift&amp;#96; to check both:\\n1. **Location change criteria** (existing): Distance/accuracy thresholds\\n2. **Time-based criteria** (new): Time elapsed since last server update\\n\\n## Implementation Details\\n\\n### 1. Add Setting for Periodic Update Interval\\n\\n**File**: &amp;#96;miataru/SettingsManagers/App Settings/SettingsManager.swift&amp;#96;\\n\\n- Add new &amp;#96;@Published&amp;#96; property &amp;#96;periodicLocationUpdateIntervalHo [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 14138,
                  "content": "  \"overview\": \"Add time-based periodic location updates to the Miataru server. Currently, updates are only sent when location changes significantly. This plan adds a configurable time interval (1-24 hours) so updates are sent periodically even if location hasn't changed, ensuring battery level and other data stay current.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 15032,
                  "content": "The implementation ensures that location updates (including battery level and other metadata) are sent to the server periodically based on the user-configured interval, even when the device is stationary. The time-based check works alongside the existing distance/accuracy-based criteria, so updates are sent when either condition is met."
                },

                {
                  "lineNumber": 24804,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 24894,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 24898,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 24909,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 28897,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"- Add other devices by scanning their Miataru QR code.\\n- The QR tab offers one‑tap sharing, and the add‑device sheet guides scanning and rejects non‑Miataru codes.\\n\\n- The share sheet includes additional options, and email sharing attaches the QR image reliably.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&amp;#96; renders customizable QR codes using the &amp;#96;QRCode&amp;#96; package and supports &amp;#96;ShareLink&amp;#96; and &amp;#96;MFMailComposeViewController&amp;#96;.\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_AddDeviceView&amp;#96; validates the &amp;#96;miataru://&amp;#96; prefix from scanned codes before accepting an ID and allows manual entry with color selection.\\n\\n## Onboarding Flow\\n**For users:**\\n- A six‑step wizard guides through welcome, permissions, server URL, history settings, personal QR code display, and completion.\\n- Each step shows illustrations and contextual explanations; server selection validates custom HTTPS URLs, and completion flag controls whether the wizard reappears on next launc [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 28991,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- New options include: navigation route auto‑update, route progress visualization toggle, a global pulsing/shimmer switch for map markers, and off‑screen arrow visibility.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 29463,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# Cursor Rules for miataru iOS App\\n\\n## Project Context\\nThis is an open-source iOS application for privacy-friendly location tracking, sharing, and device management. Built with SwiftUI and modern iOS frameworks (iOS 18 and iOS 26).\\n\\n## Code Style &amp;amp; Standards\\n- Use SwiftUI best practices\\n- Follow iOS Human Interface Guidelines\\n- Maintain privacy-first approach\\n- Use English for all code comments and strings\\n- Implement proper error handling and battery optimization\\n\\n## Architecture Guidelines\\n- Use ObservableObject and @Published for state management\\n- Keep views lightweight and delegate business logic to managers\\n- Implement proper MVVM pattern\\n- Use UserDefaults for settings persistence\\n- Handle location permissions gracefully\\n\\n## Key Components\\n- LocationManager: Handles location tracking and permissions\\n- SettingsManager: Manages user preferences\\n- Device management and QR code functionality\\n- Multi-platform support (iPhone, iPad, Mac) [... omitted end of long line]"
                },

                  "lineNumber": 87,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru iOS App - Project Overview\\n\\n## 🎯 Project Purpose\\nmiataru is a privacy-focused iOS application that enables users to track their device location, share it securely with trusted parties, and manage multiple devices and groups. The app prioritizes user privacy, battery efficiency, and cross-platform compatibility.\\n\\n## 🏗️ Architecture Overview\\n\\n### Technology Stack\\n- **Frontend**: SwiftUI (iOS 18.0+)\\n- **State Management**: ObservableObject pattern with @Published properties\\n- **Data Persistence**: UserDefaults via SettingsManager; Application Support files for devices/groups\\n- **Location Services**: CoreLocation framework (foreground and significant-change background)\\n- **QR Code**: CodeScanner (scan), QRCode (generate)\\n- **Platforms**: iPhone and iPad\\n\\n### Core Components\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\nmiataruApp.swift (Entry Point)\\n├── MiataruRootView (Main Navigation)\\n├── OnboardingContainerView (User Setup)\\n├── LocationManagers/\\n│   └── LocationMana [... omitted end of long line]"

                {
                  "lineNumber": 102,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"miataru is a privacy-focused iOS application that enables users to track their device location, share it securely with trusted parties, and manage multiple devices and groups. The app prioritizes user privacy, battery efficiency, and cross-platform compatibility.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 265,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 355,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 359,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 370,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\","
                },

                  "lineNumber": 1165,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# Cursor Rules for miataru iOS App\\n\\n## Project Context\\nThis is an open-source iOS application for privacy-friendly location tracking, sharing, and device management. Built with SwiftUI and modern iOS frameworks (iOS 18 and iOS 26).\\n\\n## Code Style &amp;amp; Standards\\n- Use SwiftUI best practices\\n- Follow iOS Human Interface Guidelines\\n- Maintain privacy-first approach\\n- Use English for all code comments and strings\\n- Implement proper error handling and battery optimization\\n\\n## Architecture Guidelines\\n- Use ObservableObject and @Published for state management\\n- Keep views lightweight and delegate business logic to managers\\n- Implement proper MVVM pattern\\n- Use UserDefaults for settings persistence\\n- Handle location permissions gracefully\\n\\n## Key Components\\n- LocationManager: Handles location tracking and permissions\\n- SettingsManager: Manages user preferences\\n- Device management and QR code functionality\\n- Multi-platform support (iPhone, iPad, Mac) [... omitted end of long line]"

The app prioritizes user privacy, battery efficiency, and cross-platform compatibility.\\n\\n## 🏗️ Architecture Overview\\n\\n### Technology Stack\\n- **Frontend**: SwiftUI (iOS 18.0+)\\n- **State Management**: ObservableObject pattern with @Published properties\\n- **Data Persistence**: UserDefaults via SettingsManager; Application Support files for devices/groups\\n- **Location Services**: CoreLocation framework (foreground and significant-change background)\\n- **QR Code**: CodeScanner (scan), QRCode (generate)\\n- **Platforms**: iPhone and iPad\\n\\n### Core Components\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\nmiataruApp.swift (Entry Point)\\n├── MiataruRootView (Main Navigation)\\n├── OnboardingContainerView (User Setup)\\n├── LocationManagers/\\n│   └── LocationMana [... omitted end of long line]"

                  "lineNumber": 10958,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru iOS App - Project Overview\\n\\n## 🎯 Project Purpose\\nmiataru is a privacy-focused iOS application that enables users to track their device location, share it securely with trusted parties, and manage multiple devices and groups. The app prioritizes user privacy, battery efficiency, and cross-platform compatibility.\\n\\n## 🏗️ Architecture Overview\\n\\n### Technology Stack\\n- **Frontend**: SwiftUI (iOS 18.0+)\\n- **State Management**: ObservableObject pattern with @Published properties\\n- **Data Persistence**: UserDefaults via SettingsManager; Application Support files for devices/groups\\n- **Location Services**: CoreLocation framework (foreground and significant-change background)\\n- **QR Code**: CodeScanner (scan), QRCode (generate)\\n- **Platforms**: iPhone and iPad\\n\\n### Core Components\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\nmiataruApp.swift (Entry Point)\\n├── MiataruRootView (Main Navigation)\\n├── OnboardingContainerView (User Setup)\\n├── LocationManagers/\\n│   └── LocationMana [... omitted end of long line]"
                },

                  "lineNumber": 10973,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"miataru is a privacy-focused iOS application that enables users to track their device location, share it securely with trusted parties, and manage multiple devices and groups. The app prioritizes user privacy, battery efficiency, and cross-platform compatibility.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 12225,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# Cursor Rules for miataru iOS App\\n\\n## Project Context\\nThis is an open-source iOS application for privacy-friendly location tracking, sharing, and device management. Built with SwiftUI and modern iOS frameworks (iOS 18 and iOS 26).\\n\\n## Code Style &amp;amp; Standards\\n- Use SwiftUI best practices\\n- Follow iOS Human Interface Guidelines\\n- Maintain privacy-first approach\\n- Use English for all code comments and strings\\n- Implement proper error handling and battery optimization\\n\\n## Architecture Guidelines\\n- Use ObservableObject and @Published for state management\\n- Keep views lightweight and delegate business logic to managers\\n- Implement proper MVVM pattern\\n- Use UserDefaults for settings persistence\\n- Handle location permissions gracefully\\n\\n## Key Components\\n- LocationManager: Handles location tracking and permissions\\n- SettingsManager: Manages user preferences\\n- Device management and QR code functionality\\n- Multi-platform support (iPhone, iPad, Mac) [... omitted end of long line]"

Empty states guide first‑time use, and swiping a group row reveals delete or edit actions.\\n\\n- Group detail lists show each device’s last update, distance, and battery status where available.                   "lineNumber": 1656,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru iOS App - Project Overview\\n\\n## 🎯 Project Purpose\\nmiataru is a privacy-focused iOS application that enables users to track their device location, share it securely with trusted parties, and manage multiple devices and groups. The app prioritizes user privacy, battery efficiency, and cross-platform compatibility.\\n\\n## 🏗️ Architecture Overview\\n\\n### Technology Stack\\n- **Frontend**: SwiftUI (iOS 18.0+)\\n- **State Management**: ObservableObject pattern with @Published properties\\n- **Data Persistence**: UserDefaults via SettingsManager; Application Support files for devices/groups\\n- **Location Services**: CoreLocation framework (foreground and significant-change background)\\n- **QR Code**: CodeScanner (scan), QRCode (generate)\\n- **Platforms**: iPhone and iPad\\n\\n### Core Components\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\nmiataruApp.swift (Entry Point)\\n├── MiataruRootView (Main Navigation)\\n├── OnboardingContainerView (User Setup)\\n├── LocationManagers/\\n│   └── LocationMana [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1671,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"miataru is a privacy-focused iOS application that enables users to track their device location, share it securely with trusted parties, and manage multiple devices and groups. The app prioritizes user privacy, battery efficiency, and cross-platform compatibility.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 3213,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 3303,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 3307,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 3318,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\","
                }
              ]
            },
            {
              "file": "./.specstory/history/2026-01-14_20-17Z-macos-native-app-development-plan.md",

When the dark file is stale, it triggers a refresh, but the view uses a light snapshot. To reduce frequent updates and battery drain, I should adjust the &amp;#96;needsSnapshotRefresh&amp;#96; function to check only the current color scheme.                   "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]"

                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 4657,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;DeviceLocationCacheStore&amp;#96; caches coordinates, manages a centralized reverse‑geocoding queue with a configurable distance threshold, and stores results in &amp;#96;Application Support&amp;#96;. Views consult the cache first before hitting the network and throttle UI updates to the configured map update interval.\\n- Own‑device updates trigger immediate cache writes to kick off reverse geocoding promptly. A &amp;#96;RouteCacheStore&amp;#96; caches routes by device and transport, with distance‑based invalidation.\\n- Static map elements such as &amp;#96;MiataruMapMarker&amp;#96; and &amp;#96;DeviceNameLabel&amp;#96; are rasterized and cached with keys that include color scheme and display scale; renderers respect Dynamic Type and set &amp;#96;isOpaque=false&amp;#96; where appropriate.\\n\\n## Haptic Feedback and UI Enhancements\\n**For users:**\\n- Actions like successful refresh trigger subtle haptic feedback, pulsing accuracy circles show location precision, and shimmering indica [... omitted end of long line]"
                },

                  "lineNumber": 4695,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- Animations for pulsing/shimmer are automatically reduced in Low Power Mode or when the app is backgrounded to save energy.\","
                }
              ]

                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 910,
                  "content": "The user asked how to disable pulsing/shimmer in Low Power Mode or in the background. I'll provide concise steps and code suggestions. In the given repository, &#96;settings.pulsingMapMarkers&#96; controls the pulsing, while shimmer is applied to timestamps with &#96;.shimmering(active: settings.pulsingMapMarkers &amp;&amp; isLoading)&#96;."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 912,
                  "content": "To disable these features when in Low Power Mode or the background, we can monitor &#96;ProcessInfo.processInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled&#96; and check the scene phase. We'll introduce &#96;@Environment(\\.scenePhase)&#96; to manage this effectively."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 913,
                  "content": "**Configuring low power mode settings**"
                },

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Diagnosing animation gating issues**

The user reports animations persist in battery-saving mode though shimmering is gated only in Shimmer.swift; pulsing might be uncontrolled elsewhere. The environment value controls shimmering, but other animations or custom shimmer usages may ignore it. Ensuring all animations including pulsing check the shared gating environment and that ShimmerGate correctly updates it on mode changes is key to fix this.
**Clarifying low power gating limits**

The low power mode gating currently applies only to shimmering via ShimmerGate, while pulsing animations like PulsingAccuracyCircle remain unaffected, which likely causes the user to still see animations. The map annotations using shimmer might not fully update environment changes due to MapKit caching, so verifying if ShimmerGate wraps those views is important. I’ll suggest inspecting pulsing usage, centralizing gating via an environment key reused for all animations, and ensuring low power notifications update state correctly for stopping animations on mode change.</details></think>

---

You’re right to expect Low Power Mode to disable both shimmer and pulsing, but in the current code only the shimmer path is actually gated. The pulsing animation is always active, which matches what you’re seeing.

What I found:

- **Shimmer is gated by Low Power Mode and scene phase** via `ShimmerGate`. It listens to `NSProcessInfoPowerStateDidChange` and sets an environment flag that `ConditionalShimmer` uses.  
```180:207:miataru/views/Common/Map/Shimmer.swift
private struct ShimmerGate: ViewModifier {
    @Environment(\.scenePhase) private var scenePhase
    @State private var isLowPowerMode = ProcessInfo.processInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled

    let active: Bool

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .onReceive(NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for: Notification.Name.NSProcessInfoPowerStateDidChange)) { _ in
                isLowPowerMode = ProcessInfo.processInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled
            }
            .environment(\.shimmeringAllowed, active && scenePhase == .active && !isLowPowerMode)
    }
}

private struct ConditionalShimmer: ViewModifier {
    @Environment(\.shimmeringAllowed) private var shimmeringAllowed

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        if active && shimmeringAllowed {
            content.modifier(Shimmer(...))
        } else {
            content
        }
    }
}
```

- **Pulsing accuracy circles are not gated**. They animate unconditionally once the view appears, which is likely the “animation still shown” in Low Power Mode.  
```123:149:miataru/views/Common/Map/PulsingAccuracyCircle.swift
Circle()
    .opacity(halo1Opacity)
    .scaleEffect(isPulsing ? haloMaxScale : 1.0)
    .animation(easeGently.delay(halo1Delay), value: isPulsing)

Circle()
    .opacity(halo2Opacity)
    .scaleEffect(isPulsing ? haloMaxScale : 1.0)
    .animation(easeGently.delay(halo2Delay), value: isPulsing)
...
.onAppear {
    withAnimation {
        isPulsing.toggle()
    }
}
```

### Why Low Power Mode still shows animation
- The shimmering effect *should* stop via `ShimmerGate`, but the **pulsing animation doesn’t have any Low Power gating**, so it keeps animating even in battery saving mode.
- If you’re specifically seeing shimmer still animate, then it’s likely one of these:
  - You’re seeing the pulsing circles and assuming it’s shimmer.
  - The shimmer is inside a Map annotation (MapKit can be finicky about view updates); worth verifying by temporarily disabling `pulsingMapMarkers` in settings to confirm which effect persists.

### Recommended fix (guidance only)
To align with the requirement, I’d gate **pulsing** the same way shimmer is gated. Two straightforward approaches:

1. **Add a shared “animations allowed” environment flag** (like `shimmeringAllowed`) and use it in `PulsingAccuracyCircle` to:
   - Skip the `.animation` modifiers, and
   - Keep `isPulsing` false when Low Power Mode is on or scene is backgrounded.

2. **Gate at the call sites** (where `PulsingAccuracyCircle` is used) by checking Low Power Mode before rendering the pulsing view.

If you want, I can help sketch the exact changes—but since we’re in Ask mode, I can only describe them. If you’d like me to implement the fix, switch to Agent mode.

_**Agent (model gpt-5.2-codex, mode Agent)**_

Here’s what it would take to gate **all** animations/transitions when Low Power Mode is on:

- **Define a single “animations allowed” gate** driven by:
  - `ProcessInfo.processInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled`
  - `scenePhase == .active`
- **Expose it via an Environment value** (e.g., `animationsAllowed`) so every view can read it without extra plumbing.
- **Centralize in one place** (e.g., a root view modifier or app entry point) so it’s applied consistently.

Then apply it in three layers:

1. **SwiftUI animations on state changes**  
   Any `.animation(..., value:)` should switch to `nil` when Low Power Mode is on:
   ```swift
   .animation(animationsAllowed ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.3) : nil, value: someState)
   ```

2. **Explicit animation blocks**  
   Any `withAnimation { ... }` should be conditional:
   ```swift
   if animationsAllowed {
       withAnimation { state.toggle() }
   } else {
       state.toggle()
   }
   ```

3. **Repeated/continuous animations**  
   For components that animate forever (e.g., pulsing, shimmer), skip the effect entirely or render a static variant when `animationsAllowed == false`.

In this codebase, you’d need to:
- **Create the shared gate** once (likely next to `ShimmerGate`).
- **Audit map views and common components** for `.animation` and `withAnimation` (e.g., `iPhone_DeviceMapView`, `iPad_DeviceMapView`, `PulsingAccuracyCircle`, `Shimmer`).
- **Decide how aggressive the gating is** (hide vs. static). You already said “hide” for shimmer/pulsing; for general transitions you may prefer “no animation” but still render the end state.

If you want, I can map the exact files and animation calls that would need to be gated.

---

Added a global Low Power/scene-phase animation gate and wired it through the app, then conditioned shimmer, pulsing, and every remaining animation/transition to respect it. This includes map movements, overlays, playback UI, and offscreen arrows, plus the overlay managers now accept `animationsAllowed` so they don’t animate when Low Power Mode is on. Key changes are in `miataru/miataruApp.swift`, `miataru/views/Common/Map/Shimmer.swift`, `miataru/views/Common/Map/PulsingAccuracyCircle.swift`, and the map/history views across iPhone/iPad.

Tests not run (no local test command). If you want, I can run a quick manual verification checklist or hook this into a simple debug toggle.

+        modifier(AnimationsGate())
     }
